title: pkix-revocation-http: cargo doc --no-default-features has 24 broken intra-doc links
description:
RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p pkix-revocation-http --no-default-features --no-deps fails with 24 unresolved intra-doc links. The crate-level module documentation and several item docs link to types that only exist behind the crl, ocsp, async or client-* features -- HttpCrlFetcher, HttpOcspFetcher, CachedHttpCrlFetcher, InMemoryCache, RevocationCache, AsyncRevocationFetcher, clients::reqwest::ReqwestFetcher, and the bare 'ureq' / 'reqwest' crate links among them.

Not a CI risk today: quality-gates runs cargo doc only with --all-features, and docs.rs is configured with all-features in [package.metadata.docs.rs], so the rendered documentation is correct. It shows up only for a consumer who builds docs for their own feature selection.

Measured at 24 on 1ac1606d (before the PKIX-cr8 work) and 24 after, so nothing in that epic added to it -- DEFAULT_MAX_URLS_PER_CHECK was gated on any(crl, ocsp) specifically to keep it from becoming the 25th.

Fix is mechanical: either gate the doc text alongside the items it references, or wrap the feature-conditional links so they degrade to plain code spans. Worth doing in one pass rather than piecemeal.

Sibling crates likely have the same condition; worth checking pkix-aia-http and pkix-chain while in there.
close_reason:
Fixed across five crates, not one. The bead guessed pkix-aia-http and pkix-chain as the likely siblings; both are clean. Surveying every crate found the real set: pkix-revocation-http 36 unresolved links, pkix-revocation 7, pkix-mta-sts 2, pkix-tlsrpt 1, pkix-path 1 -- 47 in total, all under a feature selection narrower than all-features.

The count for pkix-revocation-http was 24 when filed and is 36 now, because the PKIX-f1j4 documentation pass (the feature table, the non-Clone verifier guidance) added more links to gated items. It was accumulating, which is the argument for fixing it rather than deferring again.

Every one is prose naming a feature-gated item -- HttpCrlFetcher, CrlChecker, InMemoryPolicyStore, DefaultVerifier, pkix_mta_sts_http::FetchError -- from documentation that is always present. None is a typo or a reference to something nonexistent, so there was nothing to repair in the links themselves.

Each crate now allows rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links exactly where the lint cannot distinguish a gated item from a mistake, scoped by the precise features the links depend on, and keeps denying it everywhere else. Verified by injecting a deliberate typo into a link to a gated item: the all-features build still fails on it (exit 101) and only the narrow build absorbs it. So no signal is lost -- a mistyped link is broken with every feature enabled too, and all-features is what the gate runs under RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings.

Rejected the two alternatives the bead suggested. Demoting links to code spans costs every docs.rs reader a working link to spare a configuration nobody publishes from. Conditional prose means ~40 lines of '//!' per crate rewritten as cfg_attr(doc = ...) with escaping, leaving the docs painful to edit.

No CI step added, deliberately: a future link to a gated item resolves under all-features and is allowed under a narrow selection, so it cannot regress, and anything genuinely wrong still fails the gated build. Adding a job would be ceremony.

Verified: cargo doc clean for 10 feature selections of pkix-revocation-http plus all-features; doc and no-std builds clean for all five crates; workspace clippy, rustdoc, 2316 tests, typos and the --depth 2 feature powerset all green under RUSTFLAGS and RUSTDOCFLAGS both -D warnings. Commit edaf66b8.
